summary.title: Alignment review: stakeholder-safe release handoff
summary.detail: A derived, read-only view of the current dossier. It preserves evidence, uncertainty, and review findings for a human decision.

goals.title: Expose evidence before a decision
goals.detail: Present goals, behavior, architecture, and findings without turning them into a semantic certificate.

goals.title: Keep consent separate
goals.detail: The Site presents; the host conversation carries the explicit human decision.

evidence.excerpt: The manifest identifies the project, current workflow phase, and exact human-authored files included in the reviewed snapshot.
The charter defines the stakeholder problem, desired outcome, scope boundary, non-goals, constraints, and decision authority.
Stakeholders need inspectable evidence and visible uncertainty before deciding whether the dossier is an adequate basis for downstream work.
Independent review records semantic gaps and accepted limitations for human judgment; it does not certify correctness.
The review sponsor is accountable for deciding whether the presented evidence and limitations are sufficient for handoff.
The delivery team authors canonical artifacts and owns revisions requested during stakeholder review.
The sponsor reviews goals, examples, responsibilities, decisions, and findings, then decides outside the Site.
When an open finding exists, the review presents it before snapshot readiness so the limitation cannot be hidden by a ready badge.
Proposed, assumed, open, and conflicting claims remain visibly labelled in text wherever they appear.
The review Site is a read-only presentation between canonical dossier evidence and the human decision channel.
The presentation container renders supplied review data but owns no approval state or semantic authority.
Canonical dossier files remain the source of truth; the derived Site can be rebuilt without changing them.
ADR-01 keeps approval outside the renderer so a Site interaction cannot impersonate a current human decision.
Open findings require explicit stakeholder judgment and may block handoff when they distort the decision boundary.
The stakeholder must decide whether the unresolved acceptance threshold is safe to carry into downstream design.
Two source artifacts assign delivery ownership differently; decision authority must resolve the conflict.
